name: CV / Resume Analysis
description: Signals extracted from the user's CV/resume to evidence DevOps skills. CV data provides self-reported information that must be cross-validated with other sources.

extraction_rules.description: How to extract and weight information from CV content.

sections.description: Explicit list of technologies and tools mentioned in skills section.
sections.notes: Low strength because listing a skill doesn't prove proficiency. Must cross-reference with experience and projects.

sections.description: Job descriptions and responsibilities mentioning DevOps activities.
sections.notes: Higher strength when specific actions and outcomes are described (e.g., 'built CI/CD pipeline that reduced deployment time by 50%').
quality_indicators: Specific tools and technologies mentioned in context
Quantifiable outcomes (reduced X by Y%, managed N servers)
Action verbs indicating hands-on work (built, designed, implemented, automated, migrated)

sections.description: Personal or academic projects demonstrating DevOps skills.
sections.notes: Higher strength if linked to GitHub repository or live demo. Cross-reference with GitHub analysis.
quality_indicators: Links to source code or live environments

sections.description: Relevant courses, degrees, and academic background.
sections.notes: Provides context but doesn't directly evidence practical skill. Relevant for students.
Certifications alone are NOT evidence of practical skill. They indicate theoretical knowledge and should be cross-validated.

signal_mapping.description: How CV mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Mentions Docker/containerization in work experience with specific activities
Lists Docker in skills section only
Describes building CI/CD pipelines with quantifiable outcomes
Mentions managing Kubernetes clusters in production
Has AWS/Azure/GCP certification without project evidence

important_notes: CV data is self-reported and inherently unreliable as standalone evidence
Always cross-validate CV claims with GitHub and LinkedIn data
Certifications should NEVER be the sole evidence for a skill rating
Look for specificity and depth â€” 'managed Docker containers' is weaker than 'implemented multi-stage Docker builds reducing image size by 60%'
Recency matters â€” skills used 3+ years ago may not reflect current competency
